claim: Notochord coin-shaped precursor cells are initially arranged in a simple unidimensional geometry.
source: To address this, we use the zebrafish notochord, an organ where coin-shaped precursor cells are initially arranged in a simple unidimensional geometry.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract and supported by imaging data shown in Figure 1B-D.

claim: Notochord precursor cells differentiate into vacuolated and sheath cells.
source: These cells then differentiate into vacuolated and sheath cells.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by Figure 1A schematic and time-lapse imaging in Figure 2G.

claim: jag1a and her6/her9 are the main components of a Notch GRN that generates a lateral inhibition pattern in the notochord.
source: Using newly developed transgenic tools together with in vivo imaging, we identify jag1a and her6/her9 as the main components of a Notch GRN that generates a lateral inhibition pattern and determines cell fate.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figures 1-4 showing alternating expression patterns and genetic perturbations.

claim: Lateral inhibition patterning is promoted when ligand-receptor interactions are stronger within the same cell than in neighboring cells.
source: Making use of this experimental system and mathematical modeling we show that lateral inhibition patterning is promoted when ligand-receptor interactions are stronger within the same cell than in neighboring cells.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by mathematical modeling in Figure 6J and experimental data in Figure 6B-I.

claim: Notochord precursor cells are coin-shaped and unidimensionally arranged one cell after another.
source: We observed that notochord precursor cells are coin-shaped and unidimensionally arranged one cell after another (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is directly stated in the Results section and supported by imaging data in Figure 1B.

claim: Notochord coin-shaped cells are isolated from the rest of the tissues by a layer of extracellular matrix.
source: Using transmission electron microscopy, we confirmed this cell arrangement and observed that coin-shaped notochord cells are isolated from the rest of the tissues by a layer of extracellular matrix (Figure 1C–D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by electron microscopy images in Figure 1C-D.

claim: The contacts of each notochord cell are restricted to the two neighboring cells in the stack.
source: Thus, the contacts of each notochord cell are restricted to the two neighboring cells in the stack.
evidence: This is inferred from the unidimensional arrangement and electron microscopy data showing the extracellular matrix isolation.

claim: A lateral induction network gives rise to a homogeneous pattern where all cells have both high concentrations of NICD and ligand.
source: This network gives rise to a homogeneous pattern, where all the cells have both high concentrations of NICD and ligand (Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A, Matsuda et al., 2012; Petrovic et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by mathematical modeling shown in Figure 1E and citations to previous work.

claim: A lateral inhibition network results in a NICD-ligand alternating pattern.
source: The result of this model is a NICD-ligand alternating pattern (Figure 1F and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by mathematical modeling shown in Figure 1F.

claim: jag1a and tp1:GFP show an alternating pattern in the notochord.
source: Interestingly, we found an alternating pattern (Figure 1G–M, Figure 1—figure supplement 1G, H) that resembles lateral inhibition, a pattern that has never been described for Jag1.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by imaging data in Figure 1G-M.

claim: Injection of jag1a and jag1b MOs causes tp1:GFP signal to almost completely disappear in the notochord.
source: First, we observed that when we injected the two MOs simultaneously, the tp1:GFP signal almost completely disappeared in the notochord, but not in the neighboring tissues (Figure 2D), supporting the hypothesis that jag1a and jag1b are the main, if not the only, Notch ligands expressed in the notochord.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by imaging data in Figure 2D.

claim: jag1a and jag1b are the main Notch ligands expressed in the notochord.
source: First, we observed that when we injected the two MOs simultaneously, the tp1:GFP signal almost completely disappeared in the notochord, but not in the neighboring tissues (Figure 2D), supporting the hypothesis that jag1a and jag1b are the main, if not the only, Notch ligands expressed in the notochord.
evidence: This is inferred from the MO knockdown experiment showing loss of Notch activity.

claim: Inhibition of jag1a and jag1b increases the number of jag1a:mScarlet-positive cells that are directly adjacent to other jag1a:mScarlet-positive cells.
source: We also observed an increase in the number of jag1a:mScarlet-positive cells that are directly adjacent to other jag1a:mScarlet-positive cells, suggesting that a lateral inhibition process is disrupted upon inhibition of jag1a and jag1b.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by quantification in Figure 2E.

claim: jag1a and jag1b have similar, but not completely redundant roles in the generation of the lateral inhibition pattern.
source: This effect was also observed, although to a lower extent, when injecting the jag1a or jag1b MOs separately, indicating that jag1a and jag1b have similar, but not completely redundant roles in the generation of the lateral inhibition pattern (Figure 2A–E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 2A-E showing partial effects of individual MO injections.

claim: jag1a-positive cells give rise to vacuolated cells.
source: We found that jag1a-positive cells gave rise to vacuolated cells, while tp1-positive cells differentiated into sheath cells (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by time-lapse imaging data in Figure 2G.

claim: tp1-positive cells differentiate into sheath cells.
source: We found that jag1a-positive cells gave rise to vacuolated cells, while tp1-positive cells differentiated into sheath cells (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by time-lapse imaging data in Figure 2G.

claim: jag1a is an early marker for vacuolated cell fate.
source: Having identified jag1a is an early marker for cell fate, we decided to verify if cell fate is determined by a lateral inhibition process.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by the time-lapse data showing jag1a-positive cells becoming vacuolated cells.

claim: None of the future vacuolated cells were adjacent to another future vacuolated cell at the disc cell stage.
source: We found that none of the future vacuolated cells were adjacent to another future vacuolated cell at the disc cell stage (n = 0/51 cells quantified from 4 fish).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with specific quantification data.

claim: Future sheath cells almost always had another future sheath cell next to them.
source: In contrast, future sheath cells almost always had another future sheath cell next to them (n = 221/222 cells quantified from 4 fish).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with specific quantification data.

claim: jag1a and Notch activity are the first available markers of vacuolated and sheath cell fates.
source: Altogether, these results establish jag1a and Notch activity as the first available markers of vacuolated and sheath cell fates, and confirmed that this cell fate decision is mediated by a lateral inhibition process.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the time-lapse and quantification data.

claim: her6 and her9 are the most highly expressed HES/HEY family genes in the notochord at 18 and 24 hpf.
source: We found that her6 and her9 are the most highly expressed genes of this family in the notochord at 18 and 24 hours post-fertilization (hpf) (Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A-F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by single-cell RNA-Seq data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: her6 and her9 are expressed in an alternating pattern with jag1a.
source: her6 and her9 were expressed in an alternating pattern with jag1a (Figure 3B–O).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by HCR in situ hybridization data in Figure 3B-O.

claim: her12 was not detected in the notochord by HCR.
source: In contrast to her6 and her9 expression, her12, which was expressed at a much lower level according to the RNA-Seq, was not detected in the notochord by HCR (Figure 3—figure supplement 1G-M).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by HCR data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1G-M.

claim: Several Rbp-Jκ binding sites were identified in the proximity of her6 and her9 transcription start sites.
source: Several Rbp-Jκ binding sites were identified in the proximity of her6 and her9 transcription start sites, supporting the hypothesis that these genes are direct Notch targets (Figure 3—figure supplement 1N, Ye et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by CUT & RUN data from a published study.

claim: notch2 was detected in most notochord cells at the highest levels at 18 and 24 hpf.
source: By single-cell RNA-Seq data analysis (Wagner et al., 2018) we found that notch2 was detected in most cells at the highest levels at 18 and 24 hpf (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A-E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by single-cell RNA-Seq data analysis.

claim: notch2 is the main Notch receptor in the notochord.
source: Altogether, we identified the main components of the lateral inhibition GRN, finding her6 and her9 as candidate genes to repress jag1a expression, and notch2 as the main Notch receptor in the notochord.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on single-cell RNA-Seq analysis and HCR data.

claim: GFP-p2a-her6 and GFP-p2a-her9 cells had a lower level of jag1a:mScarlet than only-GFP cells.
source: We found that GFP-p2a-her6 and GFP-p2a-her9 cells had a lower level of jag1a:mScarlet than only-GFP cells, indicating that her6 and her9 repress jag1a expression in a cell autonomous manner (Figure 4A–G).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by quantification data in Figure 4G.

claim: her6 and her9 repress jag1a expression in a cell autonomous manner.
source: We found that GFP-p2a-her6 and GFP-p2a-her9 cells had a lower level of jag1a:mScarlet than only-GFP cells, indicating that her6 and her9 repress jag1a expression in a cell autonomous manner (Figure 4A–G).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by both transgenic reporter and HCR data.

claim: her6 and her9 are necessary for lateral inhibition in the notochord.
source: We found this value to be increased upon her6 and her9 gene deletion, showing that her6 and her9 are necessary for lateral inhibition (Figure 4H–J).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by CRISPR knockout data in Figure 4H-J.

claim: her6 and her9 are sufficient to inhibit jag1a expression.
source: Having identified her6 and her9 as genes sufficient to inhibit jag1a expression, we studied if these genes are necessary for lateral inhibition patterning in the notochord.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on the overexpression experiments showing reduced jag1a levels.

claim: her6 and her9 are the repressors in the GRN that generate a lateral inhibition pattern in the notochord.
source: Altogether, we show that her6 and her9 are the repressors in the GRN that generate a lateral inhibition pattern in the notochord.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from both gain-of-function and loss-of-function experiments.

claim: A higher proportion of sheath cells is found in GFP-p2a-her6 and GFP-p2a-her9 expressing cells.
source: At 2 days postfertilization (dpf), a stage where vacuolated and sheath cells can be distinguished, we found a higher proportion of sheath cells in GFP-p2a-her6 and GFP-p2a-her9 expressing cells.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by quantification in Figure 5D.

claim: her6 and her9 are sufficient to determine sheath cell fate.
source: This result indicates that her6 and her9 are sufficient to determine sheath cell fate (Figure 5A–D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by cell fate analysis in Figure 5A-D.

claim: The Notch ligand jag1a is sufficient to drive vacuolated cell fate in the same cells where it is expressed.
source: Interestingly, we found that the Notch ligand jag1a is sufficient to drive vacuolated cell fate in the same cells where it is expressed (Figure 5E–G).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by cell fate analysis in Figure 5E-G.

claim: JICD signaling is not sufficient to explain the jag1a effect on fate in the notochord.
source: We did not observe any effect of JICD on cell fate (Figure 5—figure supplement 1), showing that JICD signaling is not sufficient to explain the jag1a effect on fate in the notochord.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by experimental data in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Overexpression of jag1a causes only a minor or no increase in her6/her9 expression in neighboring cells.
source: We found only a minor or no increase in her6/her9 expression in the neighboring cells (Figure 6B, D, E, G,I), suggesting a small Notch-ligand trans-interaction.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by quantification in Figure 6I.

claim: Overexpression of jag1a causes a strong reduction of her6/her9 expression in the jag1a-expressing cells.
source: On the other hand, we observed a strong reduction of her6/her9 expression in the jag1a-expressing cells (Figure 6C, F and H).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by quantification in Figure 6H.

claim: The main mechanism regulating cell fate in jag1a-expressing cells is cis-inhibition.
source: Although we cannot rule out that the small effect in the neighboring cells is due to limiting Notch receptor levels, the strong effect observed in the jag1a-expressing cells suggests the main mechanism regulating cell fate in its own cell is cis-inhibition.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an inference from the experimental data showing strong cell-autonomous effects.

claim: In the absence of cooperativity, patterning only occurs in a region of the parameter space where Kcis is higher than Ktrans.
source: We found that in the absence of cooperativity, patterning only occurs in a region of the parameter space where Kcis is higher than Ktrans (Figure 6J, Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by mathematical modeling results in Figure 6J.

claim: Even with cooperativity, stronger cis- than trans-interactions destabilize the homogeneous state, thus promoting patterning.
source: However, we observed that even in this case, stronger cis- than trans-interactions destabilize the homogeneous state, thus promoting patterning (Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by mathematical modeling results in Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: A jag1a/jag1b-her6/her9 network generates a lateral inhibition pattern that determines cell fate in the notochord.
source: In conclusion, our results show that a jag1a/jag1b-her6/her9 network generates a lateral inhibition pattern that determines cell fate in the notochord, and that strong ligand-receptor interactions within cells play a key role in the generation of such patterns.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from all the experimental and modeling data.

claim: Strong ligand-receptor interactions within cells play a key role in the generation of lateral inhibition patterns.
source: In conclusion, our results show that a jag1a/jag1b-her6/her9 network generates a lateral inhibition pattern that determines cell fate in the notochord, and that strong ligand-receptor interactions within cells play a key role in the generation of such patterns.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from both experimental and modeling data.

claim: Notch signaling inhibits jag1a expression in the notochord through activation of her6 and her9.
source: Here we show that Notch signaling, through the activation of the transcriptional repressors her6 and her9, inhibits jag1a expression in the notochord, leading to the generation of lateral inhibition patterns.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a summary of the main findings.

claim: Jag1 can generate lateral inhibition patterns, not just lateral induction patterns.
source: Previously, it was generally accepted that Notch signaling activates Jag1 expression leading to lateral induction patterns (Boareto, 2020; Boareto et al., 2015; Sjöqvist and Andersson, 2019). Here we show that Notch signaling, through the activation of the transcriptional repressors her6 and her9, inhibits jag1a expression in the notochord, leading to the generation of lateral inhibition patterns.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and supported by the experimental data showing alternating jag1a and Notch activity patterns.

claim: Jag1 is expressed in many tissues including heart, inner ear, muscle, and kidney.
source: Importantly, Jag1 is expressed in many other tissues apart from the notochord, including heart, inner ear, muscle, and kidney (D'Amato et al., 2016; Leimeister et al., 2003; Lindsell et al., 1995; Murata et al., 2006), suggesting that the identified GRN may be relevant for pattern generation in these other contexts.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The identified GRN may be relevant for pattern generation in tissues beyond the notochord.
source: Importantly, Jag1 is expressed in many other tissues apart from the notochord, including heart, inner ear, muscle, and kidney (D'Amato et al., 2016; Leimeister et al., 2003; Lindsell et al., 1995; Murata et al., 2006), suggesting that the identified GRN may be relevant for pattern generation in these other contexts.
evidence: This is suggested in the Discussion section based on the expression of Jag1 in multiple tissues.

claim: Hes1 is expressed in the mouse notochord.
source: Previous studies based on BAC transgenesis showed that Hes1, the mammalian homolog of her6 and her9, is expressed in the mouse notochord, suggesting it may play a role in the patterning of the mammalian notochord (Klinck et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Mutations in JAG1 and NOTCH2 lead to vertebrae malformations in human Alagille Syndrome.
source: Interestingly, mutations in JAG1 and NOTCH2 (McDaniell et al., 2006; Oda et al., 1997), the human homologs of the main ligands and receptor in the zebrafish notochord, lead to vertebrae malformations in human Alagille Syndrome.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Spine problems in Alagille Syndrome may result from defective Notch patterning during notochord development.
source: This suggests that spine problems in this human syndrome may be the result of defective Notch patterning during notochord development.
evidence: This is suggested in the Discussion section based on the connection between the identified GRN and human disease mutations.

claim: The zebrafish notochord is a unidimensional system to study lateral inhibition patterning.
source: Altogether, we have established the notochord as a new model system to study the principles that determine pattern generation.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a conclusion from the study.

claim: The tp1 promoter includes 12 Rbp-Jκ binding sites derived from a viral sequence.
source: The tp1 promoter includes 12 Rbp-Jκ binding sites derived from a viral sequence, making the tp1:GFP line a reporter of Notch activity.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the tp1:GFP reporter line.

claim: emilin3a offers the best balance between notochord specificity and high expression levels.
source: Making use of the single-cell RNA-Seq dataset (Wagner et al., 2018), we identified emilin3a as the gene that offers the best balance between notochord specificity and high expression levels (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by single-cell RNA-Seq analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A,B.

claim: The emilin3a promoter is sufficient to drive gene expression in the notochord.
source: We cloned a 5 kb promoter upstream of the coding region and showed that it is sufficient to drive gene expression in the notochord, including most of both jag1a:mNeonGreen- and tp1:GFP cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C-J).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by imaging data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C-J.

claim: Lateral inhibition has been described for Delta-like ligands and Jag2.
source: Lateral inhibition patterning has been described for the Delta-like (Dll) ligands and for Jag2 (Heitzler and Simpson, 1991; Lanford et al., 1999)
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction and supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Lateral induction has been shown for the ligand Jag1.
source: Lateral induction has been shown for the ligand Jag1, whereby Notch activation by Jag1 triggers the expression of the same ligand in the adjacent cells, promoting the same fate (Hartman et al., 2010; Manderfield et al., 2012; Neves et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction and supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Cis-inhibition is required for patterning in the absence of cooperative interactions.
source: This interaction, known as cis-inhibition, mutually inactivates both the ligand and receptor, and mathematical models have shown that it is required for patterning in the absence of cooperative interactions (Formosa-Jordan and Ibañes, 2014; Sprinzak et al., 2010; Sprinzak et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction and supported by citations to previous modeling studies.

claim: Different ligands and receptors bind to each other in cis and trans with different affinities.
source: Different ligands and receptors bind to each other in cis and trans with different affinities, and these affinities can be modulated by posttranslational modifications (Bray, 2016; Sjöqvist and Andersson, 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction and supported by citations to review articles.

claim: Inhibition of jag1a and jag1b by morpholino injection leads to an excess of vacuolated cells.
source: Inhibition of the Notch ligands jag1a and jag1b by morpholino (MO) injection leads to an excess of vacuolated cells, while overexpression of NICD promotes sheath cell fate (Yamamoto et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction and supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Overexpression of NICD promotes sheath cell fate.
source: Inhibition of the Notch ligands jag1a and jag1b by morpholino (MO) injection leads to an excess of vacuolated cells, while overexpression of NICD promotes sheath cell fate (Yamamoto et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction and supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: The cell fate decision between vacuolated and sheath cells depends on Notch signaling.
source: The cell fate decision between vacuolated and sheath cells depends on Notch signaling (Yamamoto et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction and supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Vacuolated cells contain a large vacuole that provides hydrostatic pressure.
source: vacuolated cells, located in the inner part of the organ, that contain a large vacuole that provides hydrostatic pressure (Adams et al., 1990; Bagwell et al., 2020; Ellis et al., 2013)
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction and supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Sheath cells form the surface of the cylindrical notochord structure.
source: and sheath cells, which form the surface of the cylindrical structure (Dale and Topczewski, 2011; Grotmol et al., 2003; Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction and supported by citations to previous studies and Figure 1A.

claim: The jag1a:mScarlet BAC transgenic line recapitulates the endogenous jag1a mRNA expression.
source: For this reason, and to explore Notch patterns in high resolution, we generated a stable jag1a:mScarlet BAC transgenic line that recapitulates the endogenous jag1a mRNA expression (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C-E)
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by comparison with in situ hybridization data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C-E.

claim: 98% of tp1:GFP cells are emilin3a:mScarlet positive.
source: (J) 98% ± 3% of the tp1:GFP 99% ± 2% of the jag1a:mNeonGreen cells are emilin3a:mScarlet positive.
evidence: This is stated in the figure legend for Figure 4—figure supplement 1J.

claim: 99% of jag1a:mNeonGreen cells are emilin3a:mScarlet positive.
source: (J) 98% ± 3% of the tp1:GFP 99% ± 2% of the jag1a:mNeonGreen cells are emilin3a:mScarlet positive.
evidence: This is stated in the figure legend for Figure 4—figure supplement 1J.
